games.title: Haunted House
games.note: You are a pair of eyes in a dark mansion, lighting matches to find the three pieces of an urn.

games.title: 3D Monster Maze
games.note: A Sinclair ZX81 game where a Tyrannosaurus hunts you through a 3D maze; Edge called it the original survival horror game.

games.title: Sweet Home
games.note: A Famicom horror RPG based on the Japanese film of the same name, released only in Japan.

games.title: Alone in the Dark
games.note: Polygon characters on hand-drawn backgrounds in a Lovecraft-inspired mansion called Derceto.

games.title: Clock Tower
games.note: Inspired by Dario Argento's film Phenomena; you can only hide from or escape the Scissorman.

games.title: Dino Crisis
games.note: Mikami's 'panic horror' swapped slow zombies for fast velociraptors and used real-time 3D backgrounds.

games.title: Fatal Frame
games.note: Known as Project Zero in Europe; your only weapon is an antique camera that captures ghosts.

games.title: Siren
games.note: Called Forbidden Siren in Europe; 'sight-jacking' lets you see through the eyes of nearby enemies.

games.title: Slitterhead
games.note: Toyama's first game at his own studio, about a spirit hopping between bodies in a city modelled on Hong Kong.

games.title: Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem
games.note: Its sanity meter triggers fake glitches, such as pretending to delete your save file.

games.title: Dead Space
games.note: No on-screen HUD: health shows on Isaac's spine and ammo on the gun itself.

games.title: The Callisto Protocol
games.note: Glen Schofield's return to space horror, set in a prison on Jupiter's moon Callisto.

games.title: Condemned: Criminal Origins
games.note: An Xbox 360 launch game built around first-person melee with pipes, planks and fire axes.

games.title: F.E.A.R.
games.note: Mixes Japanese ghost-story horror with slow-motion gunfights against soldiers who flank and take cover.

games.title: Anchorhead
games.note: A Lovecraftian interactive-fiction game set in a fog-bound New England town.

games.title: Penumbra: Overture
games.note: Frictional's first commercial game, set in a Greenland mine, where you drag doors and objects with the mouse.

games.title: Amnesia: The Dark Descent
games.note: You cannot fight; looking at monsters and staying in darkness drains your sanity, so you hide.

games.title: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs
games.note: Made by Dear Esther's studio, The Chinese Room, and published by Frictional Games.

games.title: SOMA
games.note: Set in an underwater research base, it asks what it means to copy a human mind.

games.title: Outlast
games.note: A journalist armed only with a camcorder explores an asylum; night vision drains its batteries.

games.title: Slender: The Eight Pages
games.note: A free game based on the Slender Man internet legend: collect eight pages in a dark forest.

games.title: Five Nights at Freddy's
games.note: Cawthon made it after players said the characters in his family game Chipper & Sons looked like scary animatronics.

games.title: Night Trap
games.note: Filmed in 1987 for Hasbro's unreleased NEMO console, then cited in the 1993 US Senate hearings on violent games.

games.title: Alien: Isolation
games.note: A single alien hunts you by sight and sound for the whole game, and it cannot be killed.

games.title: P.T.
games.note: A free 'playable teaser' for Silent Hills, made with Guillermo del Toro; Konami pulled it when the game was cancelled.

games.title: Visage
games.note: Made by a small Québec studio; it entered Steam Early Access in 2018 and fully launched in October 2020.

games.title: Layers of Fear
games.note: A painter's house rearranges itself behind you; it entered Early Access in 2015 and fully launched in 2016.

games.title: Until Dawn
games.note: Any of the eight friends can live or die; some scenes ask you to hold the controller perfectly still.

games.title: The Quarry
games.note: Camp counsellors spend one last night at a summer camp; a movie mode lets you simply watch.

games.title: Limbo
games.note: A black-and-white puzzle platformer that teaches through deaths, with no text at all.

games.title: Inside
games.note: Playdead's second game, which took about six years to make after Limbo.

games.title: Phasmophobia
games.note: Up to four players hunt ghosts with gadgets, and the ghost can hear them through voice recognition.

games.title: Lethal Company
games.note: A solo developer's co-op game about scavenging scrap from abandoned moons to meet a company quota.

games.title: Signalis
games.note: Made by a two-person studio in Germany, with a six-slot inventory and save rooms.

games.title: Control
games.note: Set in the Oldest House, a shape-shifting government building full of supernatural objects.

games.title: Quantum Break
games.note: Each act ends with a live-action TV episode that changes based on your choices.

games.title: The Evil Within
games.note: Mikami said his goal was to bring survival horror back to its roots.

links.took: Exploring a dark mansion with little light, avoiding monsters while hunting for items.
links.added: Zombies, scarce ammo, fixed camera angles and a mansion full of puzzles.
links.extra: Game Informer saw elements later found in Resident Evil and Silent Hill; other historians start the genre with Alone in the Dark.

links.took: The fear of a monster stalking you through a 3D space.
links.added: Polygon characters, a haunted mansion, puzzles and Lovecraftian lore.
links.extra: Edge called 3D Monster Maze the original survival horror game; other historians start the genre with Alone in the Dark.

links.took: Resident Evil began as a Sweet Home remake: a mansion, item management and door-opening scenes.
links.added: Real-time 3D characters, zombies, scarce ammo and fixed cinematic camera angles.

src.t: Den of Geek, on Sweet Home and Resident Evil

links.extra: Sweet Home's director, Tokuro Fujiwara, produced Resident Evil and asked for a horror game built on its systems.

links.took: Fixed camera angles and pre-rendered backdrops behind 3D characters.
links.added: Zombies, limited saves, Capcom-style puzzles and a lab conspiracy.

links.took: Resident Evil's survival horror template: puzzles, limited ammo and monsters to avoid.
links.added: Real-time 3D fog and darkness, a radio that hisses near monsters, psychological dread.

src.t: Keiichiro Toyama & Takayoshi Sato, Official PlayStation Magazine, 1999

links.extra: Toyama said Konami asked for a horror game, and he chose darkness as a theme Resident Evil lacked.

links.took: Keiichiro Toyama's early work on Snatcher at Konami, before he directed Silent Hill.
links.added: His own horror vision: an American town, fog, and a father searching for his daughter.

src.t: GamesRadar+, the collected works of Keiichiro Toyama

links.took: Silent Hill director Keiichiro Toyama, hired by Sony to make a new horror game.
links.added: Japanese village horror and sight-jacking: seeing through your pursuers' eyes.

links.took: Keiichiro Toyama's horror direction, and sight-jacking's idea of slipping behind other people's eyes.
links.added: Fast action: a spirit possessing citizens to hunt monsters in an Asian city.

src.t: GamesRadar+, the collected works of Keiichiro Toyama

links.took: A playable teaser for Silent Hills, revealed as a Silent Hill game at the very end.
links.added: One looping L-shaped hallway that changes each time, and cryptic puzzles.

src.t: Film Stories, the lasting influence of P.T.

links.took: First-person horror in a cramped, decaying house, which critics compared to P.T.
links.added: Resident Evil's resource management and puzzles, with a family stalking you in Louisiana.
links.extra: Producer Masachika Kawata said first person was chosen before P.T. came out, while admitting he loved it.

links.took: Defenceless first-person horror; producer Kawata credited Amnesia-style games with reviving scary horror.
links.added: Brought back Resident Evil's scarce supplies and puzzles in first person.
links.extra: Kawata named Outlast, Amnesia and Slender as games that revitalized a genre gone action-heavy.

links.took: Hiding and fleeing in first person from enemies you can't easily beat.
links.added: Guns and resources return, but the opening hours leave you nearly helpless.
links.extra: Writers compared the first RE7 demo to Amnesia and Outlast.

links.took: Classic Resident Evil's slow, vulnerable survival horror, cited by lead designer Gary Napper.
links.added: One unkillable alien that hunts by sight and sound across a 1970s-style station.

src.t: Gary Napper, as summarized by Giant Bomb

links.took: Sci-fi horror aboard a failing space station, cited by lead designer Gary Napper.
links.added: No way to kill the threat: you hide in lockers and lure it away.

src.t: Gary Napper, as summarized by Giant Bomb

links.took: Named by lead designer Gary Napper as an inspiration; the source doesn't say which part.
links.added: First-person survival against one alien you can't kill, on a decaying station.

src.t: Gary Napper, as summarized by Giant Bomb

links.took: Shinji Mikami, Resident Evil's director, said he wanted to bring survival horror back to its roots.
links.added: Traps, stealth and scarce supplies in a warped nightmare world.

links.took: Over-the-shoulder aiming and tight combat; designer Ben Wanat called it 'Resident Evil 4 in space'.
links.added: Cutting off limbs to kill, zero-gravity rooms and a HUD built into Isaac's suit.

src.t: PC Gamer, how Resident Evil 4 turned System Shock 3 into Dead Space

links.took: It began as a System Shock 3 idea: a derelict ship, audio logs and body horror.
links.added: Third-person action horror with limb-cutting combat instead of RPG stats.

src.t: PC Gamer, how Resident Evil 4 turned System Shock 3 into Dead Space
GameSpot, Dead Space could have been System Shock 3

links.extra: Producer Chuck Beaver said it 'did sort of start as a System Shock' game.

links.took: Dead Space co-creator Glen Schofield's brutal sci-fi horror.
links.added: Close-quarters melee and dodging in a prison on Jupiter's moon.

links.took: Shinji Mikami's over-the-shoulder survival action from Resident Evil 4.
links.added: Scarcer ammo, traps, stealth and a nightmare world that keeps shifting.

links.took: Shinji Mikami's survival horror formula: puzzles, scarce supplies and a sealed facility.
links.added: Fast dinosaurs instead of slow zombies, and real-time 3D backgrounds.

links.took: Resident Evil popularized survival horror: a haunted building, limited supplies and puzzles.
links.added: A camera as your only weapon, so you must look straight at the ghosts.

links.took: Resident Evil popularized third-person survival horror with puzzles and limited resources.
links.added: Twelve playable characters across two thousand years and a sanity meter that fakes glitches.

links.took: Eternal Darkness popularized a sanity meter that causes hallucinations as it drops.
links.added: Sanity drains in darkness and near monsters, so you avoid looking at them.
links.extra: Both draw on the sanity rules of the Call of Cthulhu tabletop game and H. P. Lovecraft.

links.took: Thomas Grip: 'The main inspiration was the first Resident Evil.'
links.added: First-person physics: you grab and drag doors, boxes and levers with the mouse.

src.t: Thomas Grip, interview, Den of Geek

links.took: Its first-person perspective, which Grip said was inspired by Half-Life.
links.added: Physics-based interaction and horror in an abandoned Greenland mine.

src.t: Thomas Grip, interview, Den of Geek

links.took: Story-driven horror encounters, inspired by text horror games like Anchorhead.
links.added: Moved Lovecraftian text horror into a 3D physics world.

src.t: Thomas Grip, interview, Den of Geek

links.took: Zork popularized the parser-driven interactive fiction Anchorhead uses.
links.added: A slow-burn Lovecraftian horror story in a fog-bound New England town.

links.took: Frictional's own physics engine, drag-to-open doors and hide-from-monsters design.
links.added: No weapons at all, a sanity meter and a Prussian castle.

src.t: Thomas Grip, interview, Den of Geek

links.took: Living through horrific scenes yourself instead of watching them, which Grip noted in Silent Hill.
links.added: No combat, so every encounter is about hiding, running and keeping your sanity.
links.extra: Grip also said even Silent Hill was built around a combat engine, which Amnesia set out to drop.

links.took: Hiding and fleeing from a pursuer you cannot fight, a design one critic traces to Clock Tower.
links.added: First-person darkness, physics doors and a sanity meter.

src.t: Game Developer, 'Beyond stealth: keeping horror gaming fresh'

links.extra: This is the writer's view, not Frictional's.

links.took: Frictional's combat-free, monster-avoiding horror.
links.added: A science-fiction story about consciousness, with more weight on ideas than scares.

links.took: No combat at all: after playing Amnesia, Red Barrels went 'all-in with the idea of no combat'.
links.added: A camcorder with night vision, parkour moves and an asylum full of inmates.
links.extra: Co-founder David Chateauneuf named the found-footage films REC and Quarantine as the other big inspiration.

links.took: Amnesia popularized defenceless first-person horror where you can only flee.
links.added: A bare forest, a flashlight, eight pages and the Slender Man.

links.took: Amnesia's world, rules and helpless first-person horror.
links.added: A Victorian industrialist's story, with fewer puzzles and no sanity meter.

src.t: Wikipedia: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs

links.took: Made by The Chinese Room, Dear Esther's studio, with its focus on story and atmosphere.
links.added: Amnesia's monsters and a mechanical underworld beneath London.

src.t: Wikipedia: Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs

links.took: A first-person haunted house; co-founder Jonathan Gagné describes Visage as a P.T.-inspired game.
links.added: A whole house to explore, chapters about past residents and a sanity system.
links.extra: The founders wanted to fill the gap left by the cancelled Silent Hills.

links.took: A first-person house that changes when you look away, inspired by P.T.
links.added: A painter's descent into madness, with rooms reshaping around his unfinished canvas.

src.t: Bloober Team, Unreal Engine developer interview

links.took: Bloober Team's psychological horror, honed on Layers of Fear.
links.added: Over-the-shoulder combat and a rebuilt Silent Hill 2.

links.took: RE2's success encouraged other companies to remake their survival horror classics.
links.added: Bloober Team's rebuild of Silent Hill 2 with modern visuals and combat.

links.took: Realistic first-person ghost horror; Wikipedia names P.T. as its inspiration.
links.added: Co-op ghost hunting with gadgets and voice recognition.

links.took: Phasmophobia popularized co-op horror where proximity voice chat makes the scares social.
links.added: Scrap-collecting runs on hostile moons to meet a company quota.

links.took: Cinematic interactive drama where characters can die and on-screen prompts drive action.
links.added: A slasher-film setup with eight friends and a butterfly-effect system.
links.extra: Asked about Heavy Rain, Supermassive's Will Byles called it a great innovator in interactive narrative.

links.took: Supermassive's branching teen-horror format from Until Dawn.
links.added: A summer camp, werewolves, and online and couch co-op modes.

links.took: Playdead's wordless, dark puzzle platforming.
links.added: A bigger, stranger world with mind-control puzzles and a startling ending.

links.took: Watching security cameras to protect a building, a link one critic draws to Night Trap.
links.added: A guard's office, a power supply that runs out and animatronic jump scares.

src.t: Critical Video Game Studies, 'Five Night Traps at Freddy's'

links.extra: This is one writer's argument; Scott Cawthon's own origin story is about his earlier game Chipper & Sons.

links.took: Dragon's Lair popularized interactive movies built from pre-recorded footage.
links.added: Live-action video of a house full of guests, watched through hidden cameras.

links.took: Max Payne popularized slowing time during gunfights.
links.added: First-person slow-motion battles and a ghost girl called Alma.

links.took: Monolith's tense horror staging, from the studio that released F.E.A.R. weeks earlier.
links.added: First-person melee with pipes and axes, and forensic tools for crime scenes.

links.took: Remedy's cinematic third-person action and Sam Lake's writing.
links.added: Light as a weapon against shadow-possessed enemies, in a Twin Peaks-style town.

links.took: Remedy's story-led third-person action with TV-style episodes.
links.added: Time powers and live-action TV episodes between acts.

links.took: Remedy's shared universe; Control's AWE expansion continues Alan Wake's story.
links.added: Telekinesis, a shape-shifting government building and Metroidvania-style exploration.

links.took: Remedy's Northlight engine and supernatural powers from Quantum Break.
links.added: A strange brutalist building to explore and upgrade-based combat.

links.took: Control's 'Ashtray Maze' music level, which Sam Lake said inspired Alan Wake 2's musical sequence.
links.added: Survival horror, two playable leads and a detective's 'mind place' board.

src.t: Sam Lake, cited in Wikipedia: Alan Wake 2

links.took: Classic Resident Evil inventory limits, save rooms and scarce ammo.
links.added: Pixel-art sci-fi, androids and a dreamlike story about memory.
links.extra: PC Gamer said its combat most resembles the Resident Evil 1 remake, down to its scarce incendiaries.
